newsitem.title: UK: Insurance rates still falling, says Lloyd's agent.
newsitem.headline: Insurance rates still falling, says Lloyd's agent.

text.p: Rates for most classes of insurance have continued to fall in the third quarter, according to the latest Market Rate Indices from Lloyd's of London members' agent Christie Brockbank Shipton Ltd (CBSL).

"The third quarter continues to reflect a weakening market in several areas. CBS continues to forecast a reasonable profit margin in most sectors, except motor, although certain classes are now becoming marginal, requiring underwriters to exercise greater risk selection."
In line with other commentators, CBS found some of the sharpest falls within the marine market.

"Hull and energy rates continue to be under pressure, with some underwriters giving strange justifications for the revised level of rating," CBS said, adding that an increase in ship losses so far this year pointed to a fairly marginal 1996 result.
Non-marine remained competitive with little sign of the situation changing, CBS said. "However, the market has maintained a sense of discipline, which has been lacking in some other areas."
Aviation rates were little changed, although CBS said that the forthcoming renewal season could see some selective increases and a more disciplined approach to business renewal.
CBS said its experience of motor rate movements ran contrary to that of other observers. "Motor rates are either going down or remaining at low levels."
A few selective rating incresaes had gone through, it said, but these had been small and were unlikely to change the market as a whole.
"The main problem remains one of competition, with many of the direct companies still seeking to establish or consolidate market share at whatever cost."
Most Lloyd's motor business is in the UK, where a number of companies have announced rate increases in the last six months.
